evidence.paraphrase: The grandfather has come to believe he is the King of England.
evidence.quote: he was the King of England

evidence.paraphrase: Katie calmly handles her grandfather's delusion by carrying on with routine tasks.
evidence.quote: She merely gave the old man his breakfast, not forgetting to set aside a suitable portion for the smoky cat, and then went round to notify Mr Murdoch of what had happened.

evidence.paraphrase: Katie is emotionally overwhelmed when her grandfather forbids the marriage.
evidence.quote: Consternation, surprise, and misery kept Katie dumb.

evidence.paraphrase: Ted reasons out that the grandfather likely lacks knowledge of Coney Island, so a claim of kingship there would be believed.
evidence.quote: It's an outside chance he'd remember all about what the Mardi Gras at Coney was, and just what being a king at it amounted to. Then I remembered you telling me you'd never been to Coney, so I figured your grandfather wouldn't be what you'd call well fixed in his information about it, so I took the chance.

evidence.paraphrase: Ted tests the old man's memory with place names before deciding it is safe to claim to be King of Coney Island.
evidence.quote: I tried him out first. I tried him with Brooklyn. Why, say, from the way he took it, he'd either never heard of the place, or else he'd forgotten what it was. I guess he don't remember much, poor old fellow. Then I mentioned Yonkers. He asked me what Yonkers were. Then I reckoned it was safe to bring on Coney

evidence.paraphrase: Katie distinguishes between the shared understanding that the grandfather's belief is false and his sincere conviction that he is king.
evidence.quote: we know that it's all nonsense, this idea of his; but he really thinks he is the king
